s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive vision decline with a posterior segment mass
salient_findings: Declining vision in the left eye
Nasal mass posterior to the lens in the left eye
Large white mass protruding into the vitreous cavity
key_facts: 20-year-old woman
Monitored for a left ciliary body mass for 3 years
Best-corrected visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/50 OS
Pupils, intraocular pressures, anterior chambers, and lenses were unremarkable in both eyes
Nasal mass posterior to the lens was evident in the left eye
Mass had grown considerably in size since the last visit
Vitreous aspirate cytology was negative for malignant cells
Microscopic findings showed a hypovascular myxoid lesion
Immunohistochemical studies showed positive S100 and patchy positive glial fibrillary acidic protein

shortlist.label: Medulloepithelioma
shortlist.why_kept: Posterior segment mass with growth and vision decline

shortlist.label: Schwannoma
shortlist.why_kept: Positive S100 staining and hypovascular myxoid lesion

shortlist.label: Neurofibroma
shortlist.why_kept: Similar clinical presentation and positive S100 staining

shortlist.label: Myxoma
shortlist.why_kept: Hypovascular myxoid lesion with positive S100 staining

shortlist.label: Glial choristoma
shortlist.why_kept: Patchy positive glial fibrillary acidic protein and posterior segment mass

raw.rationale: The presence of a ciliary body mass, growth over time, and specific histopathological features such as a hypovascular myxoid lesion with positive S100 and patchy positive glial fibrillary acidic protein staining are more consistent with medulloepithelioma, a rare tumor originating from the inner layer of the optic cup.

rejected.label: Schwannoma
rejected.why: Schwannomas are typically positive for S100 but the presence of a myxoid lesion and specific location suggest medulloepithelioma

rejected.label: Neurofibroma
rejected.why: Neurofibromas are not typically associated with the ciliary body or the specific immunohistochemical profile seen in this case

rejected.label: Myxoma
rejected.why: While myxomas can present as myxoid lesions, the specific location and immunohistochemical findings in this case are more suggestive of medulloepithelioma

rejected.label: Glial choristoma
rejected.why: Glial choristomas are rare, benign tumors composed of glial cells, but the clinical presentation and histopathological features in this case are more consistent with medulloepithelioma
